title: Sliding Window Maximum
keyIdea: Keep the window's numbers in a structure that knows its maximum. An ordered map with counts gives the max as mp.rbegin() in O(log k) per step; a monotonic deque of decreasing values gives it at the front in O(1) amortized.

approaches.name: Ordered map with counts (your solution)
approaches.idea: mp[number] = copies in the window. Slide: decrement the leaving number (erase at 0), add the new one, max = mp.rbegin()->first.
approaches.why: Each insert/erase in a balanced BST map costs O(log k).

approaches.name: Monotonic deque
approaches.idea: Deque of indices with decreasing values: drop the front when it leaves the window, drop smaller values from the back before pushing i; the front is the max.
approaches.why: Every index is pushed once and popped at most once.

quiz.q: Why store counts in the map instead of just the numbers?
options: A number can appear several times in the window; it should disappear only when its last copy leaves

quiz.q: Where is the window max in an ordered map?
Why can a monotonic deque drop smaller values from the back?
options: A newer, bigger value will outlast them in every future window, so they can never be the max
